text: Abstract scan hypothesis: Test whether LLM agents coordinating dispatchable loads via market mechanisms (extending P framework) would exhibit same convergence failures Q observed in double auctions. Feasibility 70, Gain 45. Need to verify: (1) Does P actually use market mechanisms or centralized coordination? (2) What specific convergence failures does Q document? (3) Is there a non-obvious result here or just incremental extension?

Critical mismatch: P does NOT use market mechanisms for coordination. P uses centralized LLM-based multi-agent forecasting for carbon intensity prediction, then applies those forecasts to optimize dispatchable loads (MESSs, DDCs). This is centralized optimization, not decentralized market coordination. Q studies double auction markets where agents trade with each other; P has agents cooperating to predict NCI, not competing in a market. The hypothesis conflates "LLM agents" with "market mechanisms" - P has the former but not the latter.
